items.q: Quid pater familiās prīmum facit post merīdiem?
items.en: What does the father of the family do first in the afternoon?
items.hint: the first of three verbs ordered by prīmum … tum … dēnique

items.en: When is the grain reaped?
items.hint: an ablative of time when (no preposition)

items.en: How does the farmer scatter the seed?
items.hint: an ablative of means (with what)

items.en: How is the grain reaped?
items.hint: an ablative of instrument with a passive verb

items.en: What instrument does the one who ploughs use?
items.hint: ūtor (a deponent) takes the ablative

items.en: Who taught the Latins to cultivate fields?
items.hint: the nominative subject; docēre takes an accusative person plus an infinitive

items.q: Unde Sāturnus ā fīliō suō pulsus est?
items.en: From where was Saturn driven out by his son?
items.hint: ē/ex + ablative for place from which; Iove is the ablative of agent

items.en: What kind of field is said to be fertile?
items.hint: a relative clause describing ager; multum takes a partitive genitive (multum frūmentī)

items.en: Why is grain of lesser value?
items.hint: a quia clause with a passive verb; minōris pretiī is a genitive of value

items.q: Quotiēns in annō agricolae prope Nīlum metere possunt?
items.en: How many times a year can farmers near the Nile reap?
items.hint: a numeral adverb ('twice or three times')

items.en: Where are Julius' fields situated?
items.hint: sub + ablative for place where

items.en: Why does Julius rejoice as he watches the farmers?
items.hint: a quod clause; necesse est takes a dative of the person (ipsī = for himself)

items.q: Quandō Iūlius in praedium suum proficīscitur?
items.en: When does Julius set out for his estate?
items.hint: a cum prīmum clause ('as soon as') with the perfect indicative

items.en: By whom are Julius' fields cultivated?
items.hint: the ablative of agent after ā/ab with a passive verb

items.en: How many sesterces does the tenant owe Julius?
items.hint: a numeral adjective in the accusative agreeing with sēstertiōs

items.en: What does Julius order the tenant to do?
items.hint: an indirect command: ut + present subjunctive after imperat

items.q: Quid Iūlius servīs imperābit, nisi colōnus mercēdem solvet?
items.en: What will Julius order his slaves to do, unless the tenant pays the rent?
items.hint: ut + subjunctive after imperābō; agrīs is an ablative of separation ('from the fields')

items.en: What does the tenant beg the master to do?
items.hint: an indirect command: ut + subjunctive after ōrat

items.en: How many children does the tenant have?
items.hint: a numeral with a dative of possession (mihi sunt = I have)

items.en: Whose duty is it to look after infants?
items.hint: a genitive of possession before officium

items.q: Num uxor colōnī officium suum neglegit?
items.en: The tenant's wife doesn't neglect her duty, does she?
items.hint: num expects 'no'; the sentence also has a negative indirect command (nec postulat ut … cūrem)

items.q: Cūr Iūlius colōnum domum abīre iubet?
items.en: Why does Julius tell the tenant to go home?
items.hint: a quoniam clause ('since') with the indicative

items.en: What must the tenant see to first?
items.hint: cūrā ut + subjunctive ('see to it that')

items.q: Quōmodo vīneae sē habent hōc annō?
items.en: How are the vineyards doing this year?
items.hint: a superlative adverb

items.en: What does Julius warn the farmers to do?
items.hint: moneō ut + subjunctive (an indirect command)

items.en: Did the wolf harm the sheep?
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; noceō takes the dative (ovī)

items.q: Quis ovem ē dentibus lupī servāvit?
items.en: Who saved the sheep from the wolf's teeth?
items.hint: the nominative subject of the nam clause

items.en: What is the shepherd's duty?
items.hint: a negative indirect command: nē … nēve + subjunctive after cūrāre

items.q: Quālēs sunt omnēs pāstōrēs, ut Iūlius dīcit?
items.en: What are all the shepherds like, according to Julius?
items.hint: predicate adjectives in the nominative plural

items.q: Unde pāstor gregem prae sē agēns revertitur?
items.en: From where does the shepherd return, driving the flock before him?
items.hint: ē + ablative for place from which; revertitur is deponent

items.en: What does the shepherd beg the master?
items.hint: a negative indirect command: nē + subjunctive after ōrat (sē refers back to the shepherd)

items.en: Why will Julius beat the shepherd?
items.hint: propter + accusative, explained by a quod clause with the perfect indicative

items.q: Quō ovēs sine pāstōre relictae aberrant?
items.en: Where do the sheep, left without a shepherd, wander off to?
items.hint: in + accusative for place to which (dē viā is where they come from)

items.en: What does Julius tell the shepherd to make happen?
items.hint: fac ut + a passive subjunctive (agantur)

items.en: What does Minos pray Neptune to do?
items.hint: ōrō tē ut + present subjunctive (an indirect command)

items.q: Cūr Mīnōs taurum Neptūnō sacrificāre nōluit?
items.en: Why was Minos unwilling to sacrifice the bull to Neptune?
items.hint: the reason sits in an indirect statement after vīdit (taurum pulcherrimum esse)

items.en: What does Minos order his slaves to do?
items.hint: imperō vōbīs ut + subjunctive

items.q: In quid Neptūnus taurum mūtārī efficiet?
items.en: Into what will Neptune cause the bull to be changed?
items.hint: efficiam ut + subjunctive (a result brought about); in + accusative for the change

items.q: Quis illam saevissimam bēstiam tandem cēpit?
items.en: Who at last captured that most savage beast?
items.hint: the nominative subject of the dōnec clause
